title: Why UP's 'Aadhi Aabadi' matters more than ever in 2027 assembly election
content: Uttar Pradesh elections now prioritize women voters, who are a significant electoral force.  Women's turnout has consistently surpassed men's in recent  polls.  Parties are actively wooing women with welfare schemes and cash transfers.  Both the BJP and Samajwadi Party are making substantial promises to female voters.  Winning the trust of over six crore women voters will be crucial for electoral success.

title: Man posing as transgender sexually assaults air hostess on pretext of 'curing evil eye'
content: A 25-year-old air hostess was sexually assaulted after a man gained entry to her flat. The accused impersonated a transgender person and claimed to perform a ritual for warding off evil. Police arrested Anil Shinde, 28, within four hours after tracing his movements via CCTV. Shinde also collected Rs 200 from the victim before fleeing the scene. Authorities are investigating if Shinde has committed similar offenses previously.

title: 8-0 becomes 8-1: 'Impatient' PV Sindhu falls to cramping Wang Zhi Yi in epic duel
content: PV Sindhu's World Championships campaign ended in controversy as Wang Zhi Yi overcame cramps, a hostile Delhi crowd and the five-time medallist to snap her unbeaten record against Chinese shuttlers at the Worlds. Ayush Shetty also bowed out, while Treesa Jolly-Gayatri Gopichand and Satwik-Chirag marched into the quarter-finals.

title: How an ex-Buddhist monk & Meta engineer founded a startup that now rivals Accenture
content: Lilly Chen, a former Buddhist monk and Meta software engineer, founded Contenda after a hackathon.  She and three friends turned a pandemic-era project into a successful startup.  The company focuses on helping businesses repurpose technical content effectively.  Contenda secured one million dollars in pre-seed funding in March 2021.  Chen now leads the company as its chief executive officer.

title: Joe Root equals Sachin Tendulkar’s record for most fifties in Test cricket
content: Joe Root achieved a significant milestone by equaling Sachin Tendulkar's record for most Test half-centuries. He scored his 68th fifty during England's first Test against Pakistan at Headingley. Root and Cox built a crucial partnership to give England a first-innings lead. England's pace bowlers, Robinson and Tongue, took five wickets each to dismiss Pakistan. The team secured a first-innings lead after bowling Pakistan out for 171.

title: Meet 10-yr-old Hsu Ting-wei, winner of Silicon Valley invention award
content: At the Silicon Valley International Festival, Taiwanese innovators caught the global spotlight with remarkable inventions. A ten-year-old prodigy took home a prestigious award for crafting an AI-driven electronic nose capable of detecting hazardous substances and potentially stopping disease outbreaks. This year, Taiwanese competitors celebrated a landmark achievement, claiming twenty-four gold medals and numerous honors, showcasing their ingenuity and practical solutions that captivated both judges and audiences.

title: 2.98 lakh URLs sent for takedown; I4C flags scams, CSAM and other unlawful content
content: Government departments requested removal of nearly 2.98 lakh URLs from social media platforms. States accounted for the majority of these takedown requests, sending 2.44 lakh URLs. The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre flagged over 51,000 URLs related to various scams. This action follows widespread student protests and content blocking reports on social media. Government rules were amended to expedite the removal of unlawful online content.

title: Virgin Australia admits wheelchair user's mobility device was wrongly assessed
content: Virgin Australia has issued an apology to Shane Hryhorec after he was removed from a flight due to a misunderstanding regarding the safety of his wheelchair's power add-on motor. Despite Hryhorec's explanation that the device easily detaches, airline staff insisted on his removal. This incident unveils the need for improved accessibility training in airlines. In response, Virgin Australia is reassessing staff procedures and offering Hryhorec a full refund.

title: Six years after Michigan dam disaster, water returns to Smallwood Lake
content: Smallwood Lake in Michigan has started refilling after work on Smallwood Dam reached substantial completion in July. The refill began on August 4 and is expected to take eight to 10 weeks. Meanwhile, work continues at Secord and Edenville dams, with Secord facing a delay after crews found a problem with a spillway gate.

title: Elon Musk backs Derek Chauvin as he files new George Floyd conviction challenge
content: Derek Chauvin has asked a court to pause his appeal while pursuing new claims. His attorneys argue the original charges were unlawfully brought by the governor. Elon Musk publicly supported Chauvin's bid to overturn the murder conviction. The former officer's legal team cites procedural errors in their filings. This marks Chauvin's third petition seeking post-conviction relief.

title: Hockey World Cup: India hold England to goalless draw, seal second-round spot
content: India advanced to the second round of the Women's Hockey World Cup after a tense draw. They held England to a 0-0 score, securing second place in their group. China topped Pool D with seven points, while England was eliminated from the competition. India's goalkeeper Bichu Devi made a crucial save in the final seconds. The team progressed with an unbeaten record of two draws and one win.

title: India eases rupee trade rules, provides exporters alternative; what it means
content: Economic think tank Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI) said the change means eligible rupee payments for exports to countries other than Nepal and Bhutan will now qualify for FTP benefits and can also be counted towards meeting export obligations.

title: Delimitation, NEET & Cauvery: What Tamil Nadu CM Vijay discussed with Amit Shah
content: Speaking at the 31st meeting of the Southern Zonal Council chaired by Union home minister Amit Shah, Vijay, who is also the council's vice-chairman, sought an assurance from the Centre that states which have successfully stabilised their populations would not be penalised through a reduction in their parliamentary representation. He said the issue had become particularly important as the freeze on the allocation of Lok Sabha seats based on the 1971 Census nears its end.

title: Ashton Hall's reaction to Conor McGregor team-up grabs attention

Hall called the experience a “war with my brother,” while McGregor said he ignored his doctor’s advice to rest. McGregor is recovering from an ACL and meniscus injury suffered during his UFC 329 fight with Max Holloway earlier this summer.

title: Rey Mysterio vs Roman Reigns: Comparing their net worth in 2026
content: Roman Reigns and Rey Mysterio are two different generations of WWE success. Reigns has generated more present-day earning power from his premium WWE position, merchandise royalties and entertainment work, while Mysterio’s wealth reflects almost four decades in wrestling, licensing and merchandise. A look at their estimated net worth, career earnings, endorsements, assets and lasting WWE legacy explains why Reigns is winning the money game.

title: Premier League 2026/27: Everything you need to know ahead of the new season
content: The 2026/27 Premier League season begins with Arsenal defending their title and three promoted clubs returning to the top flight. With nine English clubs competing in Europe, another fiercely contested title race and battles for European qualification and survival expected, the new campaign promises plenty of drama. Here’s everything you need to know, including key statistics, players, managers and opening fixtures.

title: 6-year-old student slapped over homework, dies after collapsing in teacher's lap
content: A six-year-old boy collapsed and died in a classroom at a private school. His family alleges a teacher beat him for not completing his homework assignment. The incident, captured on video, shows the teacher admonishing and slapping the student. The boy was declared dead after being brought to KG Hospital. Police and officials are investigating the circumstances surrounding the tragic death.

title: India's solar story: Cell shortage may be short-lived as capacity set to tripple
content: India is set to boost its solar cell production capability in the near future. This project is designed to comply with local-content regulations and to close the existing supply deficiencies. By December 2027, a noticeable increase in cell output is anticipated, driven by new investments aimed at ensuring long-term energy resilience. The market is evolving to meet local demands, effectively alleviating supply issues.

title: 'Hi' trailer: Nayanthara & Kavin’s love story gets a twist ahead of Aug 28 release
content: The much-anticipated trailer for 'Hi,' a romance drama starring Nayanthara and Kavin, has just been released. Directed by Vishnu Edavan, this film, hitting theaters on August 28, follows Kavin's quest for love as he encounters Nayanthara, a woman challenging societal norms. Their unlikely marriage journey unfolds, offering a heartfelt exploration of love and companionship, joined by a talented cast including Bhagyaraj, Prabhu, and Radikaa Sarathkumar.

title: H-1B visa reality for Indians: Unpredictable costs, tougher odds & greater risks
content: H-1B visas have long been the main road for Indian professionals who are seeking employment, long-term career opportunities, and eventually even the green card in the US. But over the past two years, several changes in the H-1B visa application and selection criterion have added a huge layer of uncertainty.

title: No bachelors, no biryani, no dogs: What your RWA can legally ban, and what it can’t
content: Resident welfare associations possess limited powers governed by law and their own documents.  RWAs can manage common areas and enforce valid bye-laws for community well-being.  However, associations cannot override individual legal or proprietary rights of residents.  Rules must have a proper basis and be applied fairly to all members.  Disputes often arise from unclear rules and the need for greater transparency.

title: US Open sets tennis history with record $5.5m prize for singles champions
content: The 2026 US Open will offer a record $108 million in player compensation. Singles champions will each receive $5.5 million, a significant increase from previous years. Even first-round losers will earn a record $140,000, reflecting broader prize money hikes. A new player support program and a Grand Slam Player Council were also announced. This initiative aims to strengthen financial support and player involvement in tournament decisions.

title: ICC makes U-turn on Gaddafi Stadium pitch demerit point
content: The ICC has withdrawn the demerit point given to Lahore’s Gaddafi Stadium pitch after reviewing an appeal by the PCB. The Appeals Panel examined match footage, referee reports and captains’ comments before finding the pitch satisfactory. It said the surface did not show excessive unevenness, seam movement or spin. Pakistan had won the ODI series 2-1.

title: Jaayjeet Banerjee escapes serious injury after lorry hits car
content: Bengali actor Jaayjeet Banerjee was involved in a troubling accident near Tollygunge Karunamoyee Bridge when a speeding lorry collided with his car while he descended towards Haridevpur. Although the damage was substantial on the right side of his vehicle, Banerjee escaped without severe injuries. He has filed a report with the police and is anxious about the lorry driver’s well-being, urging Kolkata Police to take necessary actions.

title: Amit Shah hails South's development in CMs meet, cites 3 pillars of progress

He said that "the whole of India should learn from South India in these two areas," as per the home ministery's statement.

title: East Bengal break 40-year-old record, register India’s biggest-ever win in Asia
content: In a stunning display of skill, East Bengal FC triumphed over Rovers FC with a remarkable 12-0 scoreline during the AFC Women's Champions League. This victory is notable as it sets a record for the highest win by an Indian club in any Asian competition. The Moshal Girls now eagerly anticipate their next match against Sabah FA, needing just one more win to secure their place in the group stage.

title: Ohanna says she was pushed out: Actor alleges she was indirectly made to quit

She revealed that her departure was not by choice but stemmed from an unfortunate incident that occurred during a makeup room shift, leading to feelings of compromised self-respect. Despite the circumstances, she expressed that she has no resentment towards the show's producer.

title: 'We are Gen Z' row: Army veteran's crowdfund offer for woman to serve in Siachen

The officer offered to crowdfund her salary to serve in challenging locations. He defended security personnel and emphasized Kashmiris' equal partnership in India. The incident occurred during VIP movement which caused temporary traffic restrictions.

title: BNP's Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir elected 23rd president of Bangladesh
content: Alamgir secured 255 votes in Thursday's presidential election held at the Jatiya Sangsad, Bangladesh's Parliament. His rival, Oli Ahmed, the candidate backed by an 11-party opposition alliance led by Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami and the National Citizen Party (NCP), received 88 votes. The voting took place between 2 pm and 5 pm local time under the supervision of chief election commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin.

title: Chandigarh was built as a planned city. So why does it keep sinking in the rain?
content: Chandigarh's planned infrastructure faces recurring monsoon flooding issues. Intense rainfall exposed vulnerabilities in various city sectors and major roads. Vehicles were stranded and markets submerged after a short, heavy downpour. The city's drainage system appears inadequate for current rainfall intensity and urbanization. This recurring problem highlights the need for infrastructure upgrades beyond emergency responses.

title: Gangster shot dead outside Haryana court; 14 rounds fired, 1 attacker caught

title: Centre gives nod to set up a bench of J&K HC in Ladakh
content:
NEW DELHI: The Centre on Thursday decided to set up a bench of high court of Jammu and Kashmir in Ladakh. In a post on X, Union home minister Amit Shah said the government is "fully committed" to the all-round development of Ladakh and claimed that the decision will enhance access to justice to citizens living in remote areas. "The Union cabinet, under the leadership of the PM Shri Narendra Modi Ji, has decided to set up a bench of the high court of Jammu and Kashmir in Ladakh," Shah said. "This will significantly enhance access to justice for citizens living in remote areas of Ladakh by reducing the time required to avail themselves of the legal services they are entitled to. The Govt is fully committed to the all-round development of Ladakh and to ensuring constitutional safeguards," he added.

End of Article

content: the operation allowed 15–20 tankers to move through a southern channel of the strait each night under US military guidance . this carried close to 10 million barrels of oil a day, half the volume that passed through the waterway before the war . the previously unreported operation has provided a crucial channel for keeping oil exports moving at a time when the conflict has severely disrupted one of the world's most important energy routes .

title: NEET protests: SC sets up 5-member panel to probe excessive use of force by cops
content: the top court said a five-member panel will be headed by former SC judge justice R Subhash Reddy . the committee will examine allegations of excessive use of force against students during the student march over the NEET paper leak . it will also look into police surveillance, the proportionality of crowd-control measures, and the provision of medical assistance and compensation to victims .

title: US debt crosses $40tn but everyone still trusts Uncle Sam. But for how long?
content: the debt is now bigger than the entire annual economic output (GDP) of the country . per american, that works out to roughly $118,000; for a family of four, about $472,000. Divvying it another way, the US is adding debt at a rate of roughly $90,000 every second . the $40 trillion debt America has racked up is roughly 10 times the size of India’s entire annual economy .

title: Setback for Jharkhand students: HC stays Soren govt's order to cancel JPSC exams
content: government's order to cancel 11th and 13th JPSC exams and appointments stayed . comes days after the government cancelled the JSSC-CGL examination and all recruitment exams conducted by TDPL . chief minister Hemant Soren had announced the cancellation of the 14th and backlog examinations .
